whole_original_object.title: A two-tail obstruction to ambient conjugation in Dlab groups
whole_original_object.description: An order automorphism of a Dlab group resists ambient conjugation after every embedding, with unrestricted slopes and precise endpoint conditions.
whole_original_object.abstract: Let $G=D_{\langle2\rangle}([0,1])$ be the compactly supported, locally right $2^{\mathbb Z}$-affine Dlab group. We construct an automorphism preserving both Dlab orders and give a proof that it cannot be implemented after any embedding in either of two explicitly defined groups: all locally right affine increasing interval homeomorphisms, and all locally right affine increasing real homeomorphisms that are affine on an initial ray. The ambient slopes are unrestricted, and the embedding need not preserve an order. Perfectness separates the supports of commuting local groups; a two-tail construction handles both possible orientations of their least action components. This extends a one-tail mechanism used in prior work. The definitions and affine-germ decomposition of the standard Dlab families place them in these ambient groups. Consequently the construction gives an affirmative answer to the corrected Kourovka Problem 21.149, including arbitrary positive-real slope groups and the full and reflected extended-real families.
plain_language: An automorphism changes the elements of a group while preserving how they compose. Conjugation implements such a change by moving to new coordinates: the same coordinate change is applied before and after every group element. An automorphism can fail to be conjugation inside its own group yet become conjugation in a larger group.

This paper constructs an automorphism of a Dlab group for which that larger-group route also fails in the stated ambient groups. The conclusion holds after every abstract injective embedding, including embeddings that do not preserve an order. The slopes allowed in the ambient group can be any positive real numbers.

The construction uses infinitely many small affine bumps approaching both ends of the source interval. A faithful action can arrange the relevant local regions in either of two orientations. One of the two tails then forces a proposed conjugating map to have a descending sequence of support components, which the ambient endpoint conditions forbid.

Let $\mathcal A_I$ be the group of these homeomorphisms of $[0,1]$, **including a right affine germ at $0$**. Let $\mathcal A_{\mathbb R}$ be the group of these homeomorphisms of $\mathbb R$ that also agree with $x\mapsto sx+t$, for some $s>0$, on an **initial ray at $-\infty$**. Positive ambient slopes are unrestricted. Infinitely many affine pieces and accumulation of pieces from the left are permitted.
$$G=D_{\langle2\rangle}([0,1])=\{f\in\mathcal A_I:\text{ every right slope lies in }2^{\mathbb Z},\ f=\mathrm{id}\text{ near }0\text{ and }1\}.$$

The same automorphism works for both ambients and every subgroup of either ambient. The embedding is arbitrary as an abstract group embedding; no order on the ambient or order preservation by the embedding is assumed.

**Corollary 8.** Equip $G$ with either Dlab order. For any multiplicative subgroup $H\le\mathbb R_{>0}$, the automorphism cannot be implemented by conjugation after any embedding into any of the eight standard real Dlab families
$$D_H(I),\quad D_{H*}(I),\quad D_{*H}(I),\quad\overline D_H(I),\qquad D_H,\quad D_{H*},\quad D_{*H},\quad\overline D_H.$$

This includes the full and reflected extended-real families and gives an affirmative answer to the corrected ambient-conjugation formulation of Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.149. The standard real-line families retain their defining initial affine behavior at $-\infty$; a rank-one restriction on $H$ is not imposed.

The maps $E(f)$ fix every cell endpoint and are the identity on $[0,\infty)$. The relation $v\phi_n=\phi_{n+1}$ gives the displayed conjugation identity. For nonidentity $f$, its copies act nontrivially in every cell while fixing cell endpoints arbitrarily far left, so $E(f)$ is not eventually affine on an initial ray. why_it_works: Dlab's classical algebraic simplicity theorem makes the source group and its interval copies perfect. The affine-germ centralizer argument then separates the action supports of commuting local groups. Simplicity supplies faithful local actions, and exact finite-tuple interpolation gives a single global orientation for their least action components.

A homeomorphism $h$ with bumps approaching both source endpoints defines $\alpha(f)=h^{-1}fh$. Its interior slopes are powers of two, and conjugation preserves each first nontrivial right slope, hence both Dlab orders. The map $h$ itself has no right affine germ at $0$ and is not in $\mathcal A_I$.

Any proposed ambient implementation must act nontrivially in every selected local region. Depending on the global orientation, the left or right source tail forces its support components to descend indefinitely. Right affine germs and the initial real affine ray rule out that behavior. The proof uses classical simplicity, order and affine-germ machinery; the finite rational construction checks supplement the mathematical proof.
limitations: The right germ at $0$ in $\mathcal A_I$ and eventual affine formula at $-\infty$ in $\mathcal A_{\mathbb R}$ are essential hypotheses. The theorem concerns these explicit ambient groups and their subgroups. It does not assert an obstruction in every homeomorphism group; Proposition 7 supplies the precise larger-group countermodel.

The defining maps are locally affine from the right, with arbitrary real breakpoints. They need not have finitely many pieces on a compact interval. Fixed initial neighborhoods arising from perfectness may depend on the element; a common fixed neighborhood for a whole perfect subgroup is not assumed.

The contribution concerns the unrestricted ambient slopes, arbitrary embeddings, and the full eight-family conclusion. Historical first priority remains unestablished. No claim about the present open status of related questions is made.

metadata.title: A two-tail obstruction to ambient conjugation in Dlab groups
metadata.description:
We give an affirmative answer to the corrected Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.149. The compact-support Dlab group with slopes in the powers of two has an order automorphism that cannot be implemented by conjugation after any embedding into any standard real Dlab group. The ambient slope group is unrestricted, the embedding need not preserve an order, and the conclusion includes the full and reflected extended-real families.

The proof uses perfectness to separate the supports of commuting local groups, least action components and finite-tuple transitivity to obtain one uniform orientation, and a normalizer with infinitely many bump components near both source endpoints. One of these tails forces a forbidden descending sequence of ambient support components. A solvable affine-germ quotient treats the real-line left endpoint. The paper credits Gong, Yang and Zeng, arXiv:2609.18630, for the prior six-family rank-one theorem and one-tail support obstruction. It also distinguishes the earlier formally verified non-inner formulation from the corrected ambient question.

The six-page note is accompanied by LaTeX source, an exact-rational construction verifier, source and priority audits, and independent AI adversarial-review records. Finite checks supplement the theoretical proof and do not certify universal claims about embeddings. Literature searches through 17 October 2026 found no earlier result with the unrestricted quantifiers; this is a bounded priority assessment. AI tools were used extensively in discovery, development, writing and verification. The preprint has not undergone independent human peer review, and no formal proof-assistant verification of this new theorem is claimed. Paper, prose and code: CC BY 4.0.

Let $G=D_{\langle2\rangle}([0,1])$ be the compactly supported,
locally right $2^{\Z}$-affine Dlab group. We construct an automorphism
preserving both Dlab orders and give a proof that it cannot be implemented
after any embedding in either of two explicitly defined groups: all locally
right affine increasing interval homeomorphisms, and all locally right
affine increasing real homeomorphisms that are affine on an initial ray.
The ambient slopes are unrestricted, and the embedding need not preserve
an order. Perfectness separates the supports of commuting local groups;
a two-tail construction handles both possible orientations of their least
action components. This extends a one-tail mechanism used in prior work.
The definitions and affine-germ decomposition of the standard Dlab
families place them in these ambient groups. Consequently the construction
gives an affirmative answer to the corrected Kourovka Problem 21.149,
including arbitrary positive-real slope groups and the full and reflected
extended-real families.

metadata.title: A two-tail obstruction to ambient conjugation in Dlab groups
metadata.description:
We give an affirmative answer to the corrected Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.149. The compact-support Dlab group with slopes in the powers of two has an order automorphism that cannot be implemented by conjugation after any embedding into any standard real Dlab group. The ambient slope group is unrestricted, the embedding need not preserve an order, and the conclusion includes the full and reflected extended-real families.

The proof uses perfectness to separate the supports of commuting local groups, least action components and finite-tuple transitivity to obtain one uniform orientation, and a normalizer with infinitely many bump components near both source endpoints. One of these tails forces a forbidden descending sequence of ambient support components. A solvable affine-germ quotient treats the real-line left endpoint. The paper credits Gong, Yang and Zeng, arXiv:2609.18630, for the prior six-family rank-one theorem and one-tail support obstruction. It also distinguishes the earlier formally verified non-inner formulation from the corrected ambient question.

The six-page note is accompanied by LaTeX source, an exact-rational construction verifier, source and priority audits, and independent AI adversarial-review records. Finite checks supplement the theoretical proof and do not certify universal claims about embeddings. Literature searches through 17 October 2026 found no earlier result with the unrestricted quantifiers; this is a bounded priority assessment. AI tools were used extensively in discovery, development, writing and verification. The preprint has not undergone independent human peer review, and no formal proof-assistant verification of this new theorem is claimed. Paper, prose and code: CC BY 4.0.

metadata.title: The Minimum Distance of Unshifted Spherical Fibonacci Lattices
metadata.description: For every Fibonacci number N=F_n>=2, we prove that the unshifted rational spherical Fibonacci lattice has least Euclidean distance2/sqrt(N), uniquely attained by the north pole and the next point. This answers the separation question in Brauchart's contribution to Oberwolfach Report40/2012,p2438 (UnsolvedMath OWR-12012-001). The proof combines a global Lambert-map distance inequality with Zaremba's classical formula for the Fibonacci lattice figure of merit. More generally, a rational N-point Lambert lift with Zaremba index rho>=N/4 has exactly this minimum; rho>N/4 also gives uniqueness. The construction includes a pole and uses the exact rational Fibonacci angle; the claim does not concern the different shifted irrational Fibonacci spiral, discrepancy, or optimal packing among all point sets. The four-page written proof is accompanied by symbolic and integer regression checks and separately labelled floating-point diagnostics. This is a self-audited, unrefereed preprint prepared with AI assistance, without independent review, formal proof-assistant verification, or an absolute-priority claim.
